proposal_text:
SUPERSEDES the proposal VETOed at entry #748. That one proposed two changes to detect_repeated_veto_pattern's window; both are withdrawn. Half one did not fire on the incident, half two was ambiguous between a reading that fires nothing and a reading that converts a cross-phase detector into a single-phase one, and under the firing reading render_advisory_text would have named phase 262, which passed on its first attempt, as a member of a repeated-VETO run. The cross-phase detector is left exactly as designed.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY MISSING. Every control in this area keys on the findings-category signature. cycle_count_escalator.check_session_total counts signature recurrences against K=3; measured, the three scopes that hit the five-attempt cap this session produced totals of {1,2,2} for phase 265, {1,1,2,1} for 258 and five singletons for 261. None reached three, and that is not a counter defect: each iteration found genuinely different real defects, so five VETOs on one plan legitimately read as several problems. Nothing keys on SCOPE. Fifteen tribunal audits across three capped scopes, and the only control that fired was the attempt cap, which fires at five when the attempts are already spent.

PROPOSED SIGNAL, stated so that 'would it fire' has one answer. Add a new, separate detector alongside the existing one; change nothing in detect_repeated_veto_pattern. Predicate: fire when a single phase has accumulated at least FOUR plan-audit tribunal entries, whether or not that phase has sealed. It is evaluated on the same ledger parse, emits its own advisory naming the phase and its count, and recommends /qor-remediate. Four is chosen so the signal arrives with two of the five attempts still available.

MEASURED AGAINST THE FULL LEDGER, true and false positives both. At N=4 the predicate fires on 5 of 113 audited phases: 223 (9 audits, sealed), 248 (4, sealed), 258 (5, abandoned at cap), 261 (5, abandoned), 265 (5, abandoned). It catches every capped scope. Two of the five recovered without remediation and are the false-positive cost; one of those, 223 at nine audits, is arguably a genuine stall regardless of its eventual seal. At N=3 the predicate fires on 13 of 113 with ten recovering, which is too noisy to act on. At N=5 it fires only when the cap already has, which is no earlier than today.

COUNTING DEFECT THAT MUST BE FIXED WITH IT. parse_phase_audit_counts attributes a tribunal to phase N when the description merely CONTAINS 'Phase N'. Entry #748, the tribunal reviewing the superseded proposal, is titled 'remediation proposal review, Phase 265 cluster' and was counted as a sixth plan audit of phase 265 within minutes of being written. Any scope-keyed threshold is sensitive to that miscount. The rule should be that the description OPENS with 'Phase N'; measured across the whole ledger, tightening it changes exactly one phase's count, 265 from six to five, and leaves every other phase identical.

CLOSURE. tests/test_veto_pattern_detector.py gains: a test that the new predicate fires at four and not at three on synthetic counts; a test that it does not alter detect_repeated_veto_pattern's result for any input; a test that a tribunal whose description merely mentions another phase is not counted toward it, built from entry #748's actual title shape; and a live-ledger binding asserting the firing set is exactly the five phases above, so a future miscount changes a test rather than passing silently.

DOCTRINE HALF, carried forward untouched by entry #748's verdict and standing on entries #743 to #747: a characterization corpus offered as a behaviour-preserving refactor's safety argument must be derived from the code's acceptance conditions rather than enumerated by the author. Five tribunals on one scope failed on corpus completeness in five different places.
supersedes: the proposal VETOed at META_LEDGER entry #748
